proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current phrase that the source rank-threshold premise fails is too broad: the construction has \(\eta^{\ast}(P)>0\), so the source may still choose a model-specific threshold in \((0,\eta^{\ast}(P))\). Only the fixed choice \(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=1/80\) fails. The corrected claim preserves every formula and witness constant while stating the positive exponentially vanishing margin explicitly.

The assertion that equation (22)'s global margin is unnecessary is too strong because each fixed-dimensional witness has a positive margin and therefore satisfies the source theorem's existential threshold premise. The family proves exactly that no positive dimension-uniform constant lower bound is necessary and that an equation-(22)-controlled positive inverse-power sample bound is exponentially pessimistic relative to the constant reached gaps.

prose_updates.tldr: As an exact-real statistical procedure on the declared linear Gaussian variance-reset class, the certificate returns the environment-labelled transitive closure \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and an environment-indexed encoder estimate within \(\tau\) of the parent-supported population range class, or abstains. Its per-environment sample bound is quadratic in \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear in \(\log(1/\alpha)\), up to displayed logarithms. Separately, rational post-summary rank, repeated-eigenspace, projector-product, and singular-value decisions admit a proved polynomial-bit implementation with an explicit aggregate rounding budget. The encoder output is neither asserted invertible nor a unique representative of a repeated positive eigenspace. A legal all-dimension Gaussian family has constant reached gaps but a positive unqueried equation-(22) margin that vanishes exponentially with dimension. Consequently, no positive dimension-uniform constant lower bound on that all-subset margin is necessary for recovery, and the equation-(22)-controlled sufficient sample bound is exponentially pessimistic on the family. This does not contradict the source theorem's existential model-specific threshold premise or extend the positive Gaussian theorem to the full published class.

project_justification.fill: The project supplies an anytime-valid exact-real Gaussian recover-or-abstain certificate with public reached gaps, a sharper cap \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}<66q_{\star}u_{\star}\), environment-labelled graph and encoder targets, and explicit encoder error bars. The resulting per-environment dependence is quadratic in \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear in \(\log(1/\alpha)\), rather than the anchor paper's RKHS fourth-power accuracy dependence. It also supplies a deterministic polynomial-bit post-summary realization with total arithmetic enclosure error at most \(e_{\star}/4\). The positive theorem remains confined to the Gaussian variance-reset subclass. Over the broader published class, the all-dimension family establishes only that no positive dimension-uniform constant lower bound on equation (22)'s margin is necessary and that the associated sufficient sample analysis is exponentially pessimistic; its positive fixed-dimensional margin leaves the source's existential threshold premise intact.

prose_updates.related_work: Acartürk et al. (2024) are the strict finite-sample comparator. Their Section 5 equation (22) takes a positive-eigenvalue minimum over all subset sums, while printed equation (23) and Lemma 10 identify a projector-product quantity with \(\min_i\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\). The latter norm product is at least one by biorthogonality even though a projector-product norm is at most one, so the present proofs use the actual subspaces and the valid reciprocal witness bound \(\rho_i(G)\), never the printed identity. The positive certificate is a covariance-specialized result for the linear Gaussian perfect variance-reset subclass and is not a strengthening on the source's full smooth soft-intervention class. The explicit Gaussian family is nevertheless legal in that published class and satisfies Assumption 1 and its other non-margin conditions. Its equation-(22) margin is positive at every fixed dimension, so it does not refute the source theorem's existential choice of a smaller model-specific threshold. What it proves is that no positive dimension-uniform constant lower bound on the all-subset margin is necessary for recovery and that the equation-(22)-controlled sufficient sample bound is exponentially pessimistic while the reached gaps remain constant. The Gaussian rate has quadratic \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear \(\log(1/\alpha)\) dependence, whereas the anchor's RKHS analysis has fourth-power accuracy dependence. Sobczyk (2025), Corollary 4.5 of arXiv version 2, supplies the deterministic certified spectral-projector primitive; the present theorem adapts it to the zero/positive cluster gap, adds exact rational inertia for rank and projector-product singular-value tests, and budgets their composed error along the adaptive transcript. Varıcı et al. (2025) provide the population score-range program, and Squires et al. (2023) validate the legal linear intervention substrate.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The positive statistical and polynomial-bit post-summary theorems concern the linear Gaussian perfect variance-reset subclass in fixed coordinates on \(\mathcal S\). They target only \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and the correspondingly environment-indexed parent-supported encoder range class. The rational algorithm is polynomial after covariance summaries are available; an end-to-end raw-data implementation must also pay at least \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\) to read the sample records, so its runtime is not polynomial only in logarithmic gap parameters. The separation family is legal in Acartürk et al.'s broader smooth soft-intervention class, but its all-subset margin is positive at every fixed dimension. It therefore proves only that no positive dimension-uniform constant lower bound on equation (22)'s margin is necessary for recovery and that the equation-(22)-controlled sufficient sample bound is exponentially pessimistic relative to its constant reached gaps; it neither refutes the source theorem's existential model-specific threshold premise nor promotes the Gaussian certificate to the broader class. Actual projector geometry and \(\rho_i(G)\) replace the source's false printed norm-product identity. Neither an invertible encoder nor a canonical representative inside a repeated positive eigenspace is claimed.
